good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the following listed Conditions, surgeries/ treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Section III Exclusions > 2. Speciﬁed disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the first policy inception date. Claims for these listed conditions will be payable only after completing 2 years of continuous coverage.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer
good.reference: Section III Exclusions > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code Excl 01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered for the first 36 months from the first policy inception date. You will need to wait 3 years of continuous coverage before PED-related claims become payable.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section III Exclusions > 3. 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days from the policy commencement date, except for accidents. Any non-accident hospitalization in this period can be rejected.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-Hospitalization medical expenses incurred for a period not exceeding 30 days prior to the date of hospitalization
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered if related to the hospitalization. This helps pay for pre-admission consultations, tests, and medicines within that window.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization: Medical expenses incurred for a period up to 60 days from the date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge are covered if related to the hospitalization. This supports follow-up visits, diagnostics, and medicines during recovery.

bad.name: Room Rent
bad.quote: Room, Boarding, Nursing Expenses all inclusive as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home up to 1% of the sum insured per day
bad.explanation: Room rent (including boarding and nursing) is capped at 1% of the sum insured per day. Choosing a room above this limit can reduce the payable amount and increase your out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Expenses relating to hospitalization will be considered in proportion to the eligible room rent stated in the policy or actual whichever is less
bad.reference: Section II Coverage > Section I (after F)
bad.explanation: Hospitalization expenses can be reduced proportionately if the room chosen is above the eligible room rent limit. This can cut payments across multiple bill heads, not just the room rent.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments: The expenses payable during the entire policy period for the following treatment/procedure... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below; * Sublimit all inclusive
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered but subject to an overall sub-limit as per the table for the policy period. If the actual cost exceeds the sub-limit, you will have to pay the difference.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Expenses incurred on treatment of Cataract is subject to the limit as per the following table;
bad.reference: Section II Coverage > Section I (Cataract table)
bad.explanation: Cataract treatment is payable only up to the limit mentioned in the table. Any amount above that cap will be out of pocket even if you have sufficient sum insured.

bad.name: Ambulance Cover
bad.quote: Emergency ambulance charges up-to a sum of Rs.750/- per hospitalization and overall limit of Rs.1,500/- per policy period
bad.explanation: Emergency ambulance charges are limited to ₹750 per hospitalization and ₹1,500 per policy period. This is typically much lower than real ambulance costs, so you may pay most of it yourself.

bad.name: Implants Sub-limit
bad.quote: With regard to coronary stenting, the Company will pay such amount up to the extent of cost of bare metal stent/drug eluting cobalt-chromium stent/drug eluting stainless steel stent.
bad.explanation: Coronary stenting is reimbursed only up to the cost of the specified stent types. If a higher-cost stent is used, the extra amount may not be payable.

bad.name: Medicine Price Limit
bad.quote: In respect of medicines, Implants and such other similar items, the Company will pay up to the cost of alternate indigenous make
bad.explanation: Medicines/implants and similar items are payable only up to the cost of an alternate indigenous make. If the hospital uses imported or higher-priced brands, you may need to bear the difference.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: This policy is subject to co-payment of 20% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above
bad.reference: Section II Coverage > Section I > ii) Co-payment
bad.explanation: A 20% co-pay applies on each and every claim for insured persons with entry age 61 years and above, for both fresh and renewal policies. This means you must pay 20% of admissible claim amounts from your own pocket.
